STEP 1 - Scene: A small sushi sampler with fried tofu pieces.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A large white dinner plate with a wide rim, about 27 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- 2 cucumber maki (hosomaki)
- 2 California/crab rolls (uramaki)
- 2 spicy crab rolls with orange tobiko/sauce coating
- 4 fried tofu slabs

STEP 4 - Area:
- Cucumber maki: about 2.5% (each piece is about 3.5 cm in diameter, so 2 × 9.6 ≈ 19 cm² ≈ 3.3%; call it 3%)
- California rolls: each about 5 cm in diameter (≈ 20 cm²), so 2 × 20 = 40 cm² ≈ 7%
- Spicy rolls: also ≈ 40 cm² ≈ 7%
- Tofu: a stack of overlapping pieces about 9 × 4.5 cm ≈ 40 cm² ≈ 7%

Total covered: ≈ 24%, which matches the photo.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Cucumber maki: 19 cm² × 3 cm = 57 ml
- California rolls: 40 cm² × 2.5 cm = 100 ml
- Spicy rolls: 40 cm² × 2.5 cm = 100 ml
- Tofu: 40 cm² × 2.5 cm = 100 ml. Because the pieces overlap and are stacked, the true height is larger, so I estimate about 110 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Cucumber maki: 57 ml × 0.9 ≈ 50 g, but these are small pieces, so I adjust to about 35 g
- California rolls: 100 ml × 0.9 = 90 g
- Spicy rolls: 100 ml × 0.9 = 90 g
- Tofu: 110 ml × 0.6 (fried tofu is spongy) ≈ 65 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Cucumber maki: 35 g at 140 kcal/100 g = 49 kcal
- California rolls: 90 g at 160 kcal/100 g = 144 kcal
- Spicy rolls: 90 g at 190 kcal/100 g = 171 kcal
- Fried tofu: 65 g at 270 kcal/100 g = 176 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 280 g and 540 kcal. That fits six sushi pieces (about 30–45 g each, plus the small maki) and four tofu pieces, so it is plausible.
